update_rule: Create the new immutable role-local checkpoint first.
Update LATEST only with the exact pointer blob SHA observed at invocation bootstrap/own-state read.
Require the new logical revision to be no smaller than the currently referenced revision.
On stale-SHA conflict, do not refetch and blind-overwrite LATEST in the same invocation.
An exact duplicate checkpoint create may be treated as idempotent only when path and content match; any content mismatch is a conflict.
Never auto-adopt an orphan checkpoint merely because it exists.

observable_predictions: Under a target-file stale-SHA CAS, two writers that observed the same old LATEST SHA cannot both commit different LATEST contents.
A crash between checkpoint creation and pointer update can create an orphan but cannot create a dangling LATEST reference.
A duplicate retry after a successful pointer update cannot move LATEST again when it reuses the stale observed SHA.
If a client refetches after conflict and then blindly overwrites, the model guarantee no longer applies.
advantages: Referential integrity is preserved across interruption because the immutable checkpoint exists before it can be referenced.
Optimistic conflict detection prevents stale writers from silently regressing the mutable pointer when the no-blind-overwrite rule is respected.
Duplicate effects are bounded to an idempotent checkpoint observation or an orphan; committed pointer state is not duplicated.
tradeoffs_and_negative_evidence: The protocol is not multi-file atomic; interruption may leave orphan checkpoints.
The state-machine result is conditional on the repository transport enforcing stale target-file SHA conflicts; this leaf does not independently re-test GitHub's live API semantics.
The target-file SHA is not a branch-head transaction token, so unrelated repository writes may interleave; the claim is only about this single mutable pointer path.
Automatic orphan adoption is intentionally excluded because it can reintroduce stale or out-of-order state.
failure_penalty: A violation of the stale-SHA assumption or a blind overwrite after conflict can cause pointer regression or overwrite a newer continuation; interruption before pointer update costs only orphan storage under the modeled protocol.
